patient_case.setting: clinical presentation in an immunocompromised patient
symptoms: ovoid ulcerated plaques with elevated, pink borders on face, trunk, and extremities
physical_exam: scattered skin lesions as described on the face, trunk, and extremities

diagnostic_test.name: Tzanck smear
procedure: scraped the base of an ulcerated lesion and the inner aspect of a pseudopustule using a #15 blade
placed the specimen on a glass slide
performed Papanicolaou staining to further characterize the changes

branch.interpretation: The patient’s immunocompromised status combined with the acute onset of painful, umbilicated papulopustular lesions and ulcerated plaques raises suspicion for a viral etiology.
branch.result: Tzanck smear findings of ballooning of keratinocytes and peripheralization of nuclear material support a viral cytopathic effect.

diagnostic_options.description: A viral infection that presents with painful vesiculopustular lesions and characteristic cytopathic changes seen on Tzanck smear.
evidence_for: Tzanck smear showing ballooning keratinocytes and nuclear peripheralization
immunocompromised state favoring reactivation or severe presentation
evidence_against: lack of systemic features that might suggest alternative diagnoses like Histoplasmosis
clinical morphology inconsistent with Molluscum contagiosum or Mpox
diagnostic_options.final_verdict: Most consistent with herpes simplex virus infection

conclusion: Herpes simplex virus is the most likely diagnosis based on clinical presentation and supportive Tzanck smear findings.
